name: [WEEKLY] Dev/CI Toolchain Credential Read + Egress to Non-Canonical Registry
description: Detects a developer/CI toolchain process (node, npm, npx, yarn, pnpm, cosign, skopeo, docker, oras) reading or writing a registry-credential file (~/.docker/config.json, ~/.config/containers/auth.json, ~/.npmrc, ~/.aws/credentials) and, within a five-minute window on the same host, opening a TLS/registry connection to an OCI/artifact registry that is NOT on the canonical-registry allowlist. This fortnight it is driven by CVE-2026-59891 ("Credential confusion in @sigstore/oci can leak registry credentials to an attacker-controlled registry"), where getRegistryCredentials() substring-matches Docker auth keys and hands credentials to a lookalike registry host, and by the broader dev-supply-chain exposure theme in "The Attacker Never Sleeps, Neither Can Your Testing," "The Generator Can't Be the Validator (OpenAI/Hugging Face)" and the Gitea token-scope bypass CVE-2026-58443. It spans the credential-access and exfiltration kill-chain stages: read secret material from disk, then ship it (or authenticate with it) to attacker infrastructure over an alternative protocol. It FIRES when a build/attestation tool touches a credential store and then egresses to a registry host outside the maintained canonical set (private ECR/GCR/GHCR/Harbor/Nexus/Artifactory endpoints that don't match your allowlist land here as first-seen). It does NOT fire on normal pushes/pulls to canonical registries (docker.io, ghcr.io, registry.npmjs.org, gcr.io, quay.io, *.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com allowlisted, mcr.microsoft.com), nor on a credential read with no subsequent non-canonical egress inside the window.
